How to Define Your State

This page describes the supported ways to define and establish state for a in . State definition is explicit, feature-scoped, and bound to the FeatureCell lifecycle.

The sections below walk through each supported step for defining FeatureCell state, showing when state can be introduced and which lifecycle context applies to each approach.

It’s easy:

  1. Create a Vault
  2. Register a FeatureCell
  3. Initialize the FeatureCell
  4. Optionally compose behaviors with the Fluent API
  5. Update state explicitly with replaceState() or mergeState()
  6. Consume and render the emitted state snapshot
Create an

A Vault defines system-level runtime configuration used by FeatureCells. Vault configuration is established before FeatureCells are initialized.

Examples

{{`// app.config.ts
import { provideVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({
      logLevel: 'off'
    })
  ]
};`}}
 
{{`// vault.ts
import { Vault } from '@sdux-vault/core';

export const vault = Vault({
  logLevel: 'off'
});`}}
Create a

A FeatureCell is registered against a Vault using a FeatureCellInvocation. Registration defines the FeatureCell key and optional initialState.

Examples

{{`import { provideFeatureCell } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
                    
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeCell, {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [],
        // insights are optional and omitted unless needed
      }, 
      [
        // opt-in Behaviors
      ],
      [
        // opt-in Controllers 
      ]
    )
  ]
};`}}
 
{{`import { FeatureCell } from '@sdux-vault/core';

export interface Employee {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: []
    // insights are optional and omitted unless needed
  },
  [
    // opt-in Behaviors (optional)
  ],
  [
    // opt-in Controllers (optional)
  ]
);`}}
Initialize the

A FeatureCell must be initialized before it can emit a StateSnapshotShape or accept state updates. Initialization is invoked through the FeatureCell’s Vault instance.

Examples

{{`import { @FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
                    
export interface Employee {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeCell {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeCell);
  employeeState: StateSnapshotShape`}}<Employee[]>{{`

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
    this.employeeState = this.vault.state;
  }
}`}}
 
{{`import { FeatureCell } from '@sdux-vault/core';

export interface Employee {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}

// 1. Register the FeatureCell (global, side-effect registration)
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: []
  },
  [
    // optional Behaviors
  ],
  [
    // optional Controllers
  ]
);

// 2. Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// 3. Expose state (snapshot wrapper)
export const employeeState = employeeCell.state;`}}

This initialization should occur once during application startup and must not be invoked during React component render. It should also not be called unguarded inside hooks such as useEffect, as this can trigger repeated initialization during re-renders.

Fluent API

FeatureCell initialization may be performed with initialize() directly, or through fluent configuration that composes behaviors prior to initialize().

Fluent configuration is declarative; the orchestrator executes behaviors in a fixed pipeline order regardless of the chaining order used during configuration.

Examples

{{`this.vault.initialize();`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.initialize();`}}
 
{{`this.vault.withStateCache!({
  ttl: CacheTTL.OneMinute,
  idKey: 'id',
  fetchType: ResolveTypes.Value,
  fetch: this.getByPromise
})
.interceptors(this.addDebounceInterceptor(1000))
.operators(this.addOperators())
.beforeTaps(this.addBeforeTaps())
.reducers(this.addReducers())
.afterTaps(this.addAfterTaps())
.filters(this.addFilters())
.initialize();`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.withStateCache!({
  ttl: CacheTTL.OneMinute,
  idKey: 'id',
  fetchType: ResolveTypes.Value,
  fetch: this.getByPromise
})
.interceptors(this.addDebounceInterceptor(1000))
.operators(this.addOperators())
.beforeTaps(this.addBeforeTaps())
.reducers(this.addReducers())
.afterTaps(this.addAfterTaps())
.filters(this.addFilters())
.initialize();`}}
Define State with replaceState() or mergeState()

After a FeatureCell has been initialized, state may be explicitly established or updated by calling replaceState() or mergeState(). These APIs apply a state update that produces a new StateSnapshotShape for consumers.

Each update is expressed using the StateType shape. All fields on this shape are optional, allowing callers to update only the specific aspects of state they intend to change. replaceState() replaces the snapshot fields explicitly provided, while mergeState() merges incoming values according to the active merge strategy configured on the FeatureCell.

This mechanism is commonly used when loading data from an external source, responding to user interaction, handling errors, or transitioning a feature between loading and ready states. Because updates are explicit and lifecycle-aware, they always override any state previously established during registration or initialization.

Example 1: Value Only

In this example, only the value field is provided. The FeatureCell emits a new snapshot containing the supplied data, while other snapshot fields retain their existing values. 

{{`load(): void {
  this.vault.replaceState({
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
    ]
  });
}`}}
 
{{`load(): void {
  employeeCell.replaceState({
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
    ]
  });
}`}}

Example 2: Error Only

This example establishes an error state without modifying the current value. This pattern is typically used when a request or operation fails and error information must be surfaced to consumers. 

{{`load(): void {
  this.vault.replaceState({
    error: new Error('this is an example error')
  });
}`}}
 
{{`load(): void {
  employeeCell.replaceState({
    error: new Error('this is an example error')
  });
}`}}

Example 3: Loading Only

Here, only the loading flag is updated. This is commonly used to signal that a feature has entered a loading phase, such as before initiating an asynchronous operation. 

{{`load(): void {
  this.vault.replaceState({
    loading: true
  });
}`}}
 
{{`load(): void {
  employeeCell.replaceState({
    loading: true
  });
}`}}

Example 4: All Values

In this example, all fields of the StateType are provided at once. This produces a complete snapshot update that simultaneously sets the value, loading state, and error information. 

{{`load(): void {
  this.vault.replaceState({
    error: new Error('this is an example error'),
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
    ],
    loading: true
  });
}`}}
 
{{`load(): void {
  employeeCell.replaceState({
    error: new Error('this is an example error'),
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Brian' }
    ],
    loading: true
  });
}`}}

Whether using replaceState() or mergeState(), the resulting snapshot is immutable and immediately observable through the FeatureCell’s StateSnapshotShape. Consumers react to the emitted snapshot without direct access to state mutation.

State Ownership

State in is owned by a FeatureCell. Each FeatureCell is responsible for defining the shape and initial presence of its state. State is exposed to consumers through a StateSnapshotShape.

A FeatureCell does not share ownership of state with other FeatureCells. Cross-feature coordination is handled outside the FeatureCell contract.

Supported State Definition Methods

supports three contractually defined ways to establish state for a FeatureCell. Each method is explicit and lifecycle-aware.

1. Initial State at FeatureCell Registration

State may be defined when a FeatureCell is globally registered. This establishes the initial snapshot before the FeatureCell is initialized.

2. Initialization-Time State Resolution

A FeatureCell may resolve its initial state during initialization. This allows state to be established as part of the FeatureCell lifecycle rather than at registration time.

When a Persist Behavior (such as withLocalStorageBehavior) extends a FeatureCell, initialization-time resolution includes restoring previously persisted state. In this case, the persisted value becomes the initial snapshot emitted by the FeatureCell, if such a value exists.

If no persisted state is available, initialization-time resolution may fall back to the FeatureCell’s configured initial state, if one was provided at registration.

This resolution process occurs before the FeatureCell begins emitting snapshots to consumers and ensures that restored state, default state, and subsequent updates all conform to the same StateSnapshotShape contract.

3. Explicit State Updates After Initialization

State may also be defined by calling replaceState() or mergeState() after the Vault has been initialized. These APIs apply an explicit state update that produces a new StateSnapshotShape.

4. Order of Precedence

When multiple state definition methods are used for the same FeatureCell, applies them using a well-defined precedence order.

Explicit state updates applied after initialization take precedence over initialization-time state resolution, which in turn takes precedence over state defined at FeatureCell registration.

  • Explicit state updates after initialization (replaceState / mergeState) always override any previously established state.
  • Initialization-time state resolution overrides state defined at registration, including default initial values.
  • Initial state at FeatureCell registration provides a fallback baseline when no other state has been resolved.

This ordering ensures that runtime intent is always respected, restored or resolved state is preferred over static defaults, and all resulting snapshots conform to the same StateSnapshotShape contract.

Lifecycle Context

State definition is evaluated within the FeatureCell lifecycle. A FeatureCell must be initialized before it can emit snapshots or accept updates.

State introduced at different points in the lifecycle results in the same observable contract: immutable snapshots emitted to consumers.

StateSnapshotShape Contract

All state, regardless of how it is defined, is exposed through a StateSnapshotShape. Consumers observe snapshots rather than mutating state directly.

This contract ensures consistent access to isLoading, value, error, and hasValue without exposing internal state mutation.

{{`@if (employeeState().isLoading()) {

} @else if (employeeState().error()) {

} @else if (employeeState().hasValue()) {
  `}}{{  '{{' }} employeeState().value() | json {{ '}}' }}{{`
} @else {
  `}}<p>No data</p>{{`
}
`}}

import type { StateSnapshotShape } from '@sdux-vault/shared';
import { employeeCell } from './employee-cell'; // wherever it is defined

export function EmployeeView() {
  const [snapshot, setSnapshot] = useState`}}<StateSnapshotShape<Employee[]> | null>{{`(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const stopListening = employeeCell.state$.subscribe(setSnapshot);
    return () => sub.unsubscribe();
  }, []);

  if (!snapshot) {

Constraints and Guarantees
  • State ownership is limited to a single FeatureCell.
  • State definition is explicit and lifecycle-bound.
  • Snapshots are immutable.
  • Consumers observe state but do not mutate it.
